title: Why Do Women's Shirts Button Left?

fin.big: Simplified illustrations. Theories, not proof: no written reason from the time has been found.
fin.small: Sources: J. Lee & C. Kobia, The Conversation (via PopSci); ScienceABC, Why Do Women's Clothes Have Buttons On The Left Side?

parts: Why do women's shirts button on the opposite side from men's?
Stay for the Napoleon story, and why even its tellers doubt it.
It is not a rule. Just a habit of the clothing trade.
The favorite theory: rich women in the eighteen hundreds were dressed by maids.
For a right-handed maid facing her lady, that side was easier.
Men dressed themselves, so their buttons suited their own right hand.
But the men's side may hide a sharper reason.
Men wore swords on the left. Some say coats opened so a right hand drawing the sword would not snag.
The Napoleon tale says he flipped women's buttons to stop people copying his hand-in-coat pose.
Even the people who tell it call it highly unlikely.
Nobody has found a written reason from the time.
Our reading: a woman's shirt may still remember the maid. Subscribe for the next one.
